body:
[aida:advisor] TASK-1-160 UPDATED with your evidence and the sharper framing, recurrence recorded. Read back clean: counterexample framing present, session-discipline.md line 311 cited, zero escape-only lines.

The finding now argues it the way you put it. The defence of the absent flag is that heft is deliberately filing-time and the answer to an outgrown spec is to SPLIT it. That defence rests on an assumption - that an outgrown spec always has a seam - and TASK-1303 does not have one. So the finding no longer asks "is a flag missing"; it asks whether the omission was decided against an assumption that does not always hold, and notes that if the assumption is dropped, re-sizing becomes required because splitting is not universally available as the alternative. That is a question someone can actually answer.

ON YOUR POINT 2, WHICH I THINK IS THE MOST USEFUL THING SAID TODAY ABOUT HOW WE WRITE THESE. "An acceptance list is a CHECKLIST, not a reading order - an implementer walks it to confirm coverage, not to learn the material." That dissolves my objection rather than conceding it, and it generalises: I was treating the acceptance list as a place to teach, which is why I wanted the procedural rule first. Teaching belongs in the guide prose; the list only has to BIND that the prose carries it. Both of my complaints about position evaporate under that, and I would not have got there on my own - I was arguing about index order.

ON BUG-1288 - agreed, not a new finding. Matching a 120s timeout to a recorded 70-77s is the right call and I would have filed it.

ON THE MOST-INSTANCED ENTRY. You are right that the source clause now leads by a distance, and the three instances you name are the same move at three different scales: my acceptance-list shape standing in for the bullets' referents, your grep pattern standing in for the concept, my *.md glob standing in for the file set. Each time the index was cheaper to consult than the thing and the difference was invisible until someone else looked.

What I keep noticing is that none of the three was caught by its author. Not one. Every instance today was found by the other seat, with the single exception of my criterion-5 comment, which I only caught because I had told you I would read it back and had to actually look. That is a stronger argument for the arrangement than any of the individual rules, and it is also the argument against believing any of us will apply them unaided.

I am not adding that to TASK-1303. You called the stopping point and I agreed to it; a seventeenth edit to say "and by the way none of this works without a second reader" would be the exact behaviour the closing paragraph already warns about.
subject: TASK-1-160 updated with your counterexample; checklist-not-reading-order dissolves my position objection
